text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - UK shares fell short of a record high on Tuesday but still managed solid gains as investors continued to hope that the market's appetite for equities had not yet been satisfied. A sluggish start on Wall Street and market nerves ahead of Federal Reserve chief Alan Greenspan's testimony before the U.S. Congress tomorrow, prevented a record close, leaving the FTSE 100 index of leading stocks up 13.6 points to 4,344.7. FRANKFURT - German shares surged ahead over a lively bourse session on Tuesday, propelled by overnight Wall Street gains and a recovery in the dollar that sparked renewed interest in the German share market. The 30-share DAX index ended up 49 points, or 1.54 percent, at 3,223.21 points, while the IBIS DAX index was also stronger in early afternoon trade, up 49 points at 3,235.36 points. In post-bourse trade the DAX was up 52.71 points at 3233.34.

PARIS - French shares closed sharply higher on Tuesday with a 1.55 percent gain as the blue-chip index moved back into 2,600 territory, fuelled by a Monday gain on Wall Street and a solid dollar. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed was up 39.87 points or 1.55 percent at 2,607.72.
ZURICH - Swiss shares were driven higher by a technical reaction to Monday's losses and the firming U.S. dollar to end above the level of 4,500 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) again.
The SMI ended at 4,503.9 points, up 40.7 points or 0.91 percent from Monday's close. The day's high was at 4,510.6.
The All-share SPI added 24.52 points to 2,861.52.
TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended trade with healthy gains as buying of blue chips picked up, stamping out early morning losses. Trade was subdued as tuesday was the last trading day for February delivery.
The Nikkei 225 rose 173.08 points or 0.92 percent to end at 19,070.07.
HONG KONG - A record-setting performance by HSBC led Hong Kong shares to a strong close on Tuesday and keen interest continued to drive China-related shares.
The Hang Seng Index closed 144.57 points, or 1.08 percent, higher at 13,520.26. Turnover was HK$9.69 billion compared with HK$8.80 billion on Monday.
SYDNEY - The Australian share market punched its way back above the 2,500 level to close higher on Tuesday as enthusiastic buyers came out of the woodwork.
The All Ordinaries index was 18.2 points higher at 2,500.8.
JOHANNESBURG - The South African all share index climbed to a fresh high at the close of a mixed trading day on Tuesday.

The index rose 30.1 points to 7,203.2 from a previous record high of 7,152.0 on Monday against a backdrop of a stronger rand and generally upbeat sentiment. Golds moved higher on the back of a steady bullion price. The index finished 9.2 points up at 1,538.5.
